a: Psychology has produced several famous and sometimes disturbing experiments that revealed fundamental truths about human behavior. Stanley Milgram's obedience experiment showed that ordinary people would administer what they believed were painful electric shocks to others when instructed by an authority figure. Philip Zimbardo's Stanford prison experiment demonstrated how quickly people adopt roles and how situational factors can override personal morals, though it was stopped early due to ethical concerns. Harry Harlow's experiments with rhesus monkeys revealed the critical importance of maternal bonding. Solomon Asch's conformity experiments showed how social pressure can lead people to deny obvious reality. These studies, while ethically questionable by today's standards, fundamentally changed our understanding of obedience, conformity, authority, and the power of social situations to shape behavior.
